title: Jason Sen Explains Why Gold Is Falling Even as Inflation Rises
speaker: Jason Sen (DayTradeSignals), with tastylive host Jamal

macro_themes.view: Gold trades with bonds; rising yields make a non-yielding asset less attractive, so gold falls despite inflation.
EUR/USD's multi-year rally looks like a bounce in a bear trend with a large head-and-shoulders; dollar likely heading higher.
134+ S&P names down 40%+ on the year while indices rise; Sen still follows the index uptrend, buying dips.

calls.condition: Break of 3850 (100-day MA) means gold is in trouble; ~4000 is key support with multi-year trendlines
calls.reason: Sideways with negative bias lately, trading from the short side; 4000 area has June swing lows and 2024 trendlines.
calls.quote: If we break there, we've got the 100-day moving average around 3850... then I think gold's in trouble

calls.reason: Large head-and-shoulders after a 2-3 year bounce in a long-term bear trend, rejected at strong long-term resistance; dollar going up.
calls.quote: I think that the next big move for the EUR/USD is down. I think the dollar's going up.

calls.reason: Trend follower: indices keep going up, staying long and buying dips despite weak breadth.
calls.quote: I'm just following the indices higher. I'm staying long. I'm buying in dips

calls.reason: Host Jamal is long bonds (expects yields lower) and short gold via an expiring GC put spread to offset; Sen says yield uptrend may continue.
calls.quote: I've decided to get long. It's been rough. But I realize like I can't be long gold and bonds.

notes: Host says bond markets are closed today -> Columbus Day Mon Oct 12 (listing Oct 13). TNX call is the host's (long bonds = yields down), not Sen's; Sen thinks the yield uptrend may persist. EURUSD bearish = DXY bullish.
